Scenarios: a rulebook with its maps and parcels

Source: R/scenario.R
scenario.Rd

A scenario is everything that determines capacity: a rulebook, the parcels, roads and water, the zoning layer, and the layers the rulebook's overlays and areas refer to. Comparing plan changes means comparing scenarios, and two scenarios may differ in any of these.

Usage

scenario(
  name,
  rulebook,
  parcels,
  zoning,
  roads = NULL,
  layers = list(),
  water = NULL,
  centrelines = NULL,
  dem = NULL,
  ground = NULL,
  easements = NULL,
  other_parcels = NULL,
  buildings = NULL,
  streets = NULL,
  street_field = "name",
  neighbours = NULL,
  landholding = NULL,
  zone_field = "zone",
  site_id = NULL,
  group_by = NULL,
  width_field = "width_m",
  morphology = list(),
  notes = NULL
)

scenario_change(base, name, ...)

Arguments

name

Name of the scenario.

rulebook

A plancap_rulebook.

parcels

Parcels (or sites) as sf polygons in a projected CRS. Road, rail and water parcels should be left out (supply roads separately).

zoning

Zoning polygons with a column of zone codes (zone_field) that the rulebook's zone_map maps to zone keys.

roads

Road parcels (polygons).

layers

Named list of the other layers the rulebook refers to (overlays, areas, and layers named in distance conditions), named as the rulebook names them.

water

Water features, for riparian, coastal and lakeside boundaries.

centrelines

Road centrelines with a width column (width_field).

dem

Optional ground surface as a terra::SpatRaster.

ground

Optional ground levels supplied directly instead of a dem (from a survey, or another model): a list with sites (a data frame of site_id and ground_mean) and segments (a data frame of site_id, seq, the segment's position in its site's boundary counting from 1, and ground, the mean ground level along it). Give the segment's midpoint as x and y instead of seq to match segments by position.

easements

Optional easement areas (rights of way), for the access width of rear sites (find_access_widths()).

other_parcels

Optional parcels that are not sites (and not roads), among which jointly owned access lots are found.

buildings

Optional building outlines, for yards set from the neighbours' existing setbacks (find_existing_front_setbacks()).

streets

Optional named street centre lines for the same; default centrelines.

street_field

Column of streets holding the street name.

neighbours

Optional parcels beyond parcels that may be neighbours for a measured front yard (default other_parcels). Leave out parcels whose buildings are not dwellings, such as reserves and schools.

landholding

Optional column of parcels naming the landholding each parcel belongs to, where parcels held together are still separate sites: pieces of one landholding share their best access width.

zone_field

Column of zoning holding zone codes.

site_id

Column of parcels to use as the site id. Default "parcel_id" if present, otherwise row numbers.

group_by

Optional column of parcels: parcels sharing a value are one site (e.g. parcels held on one title).

width_field

Column of centrelines holding road width (m).

morphology

Named list of morphology settings for this scenario, overriding the rulebook's (see morphology_defaults()).

notes

Free text.

base

The scenario to start from.

...

For scenario_change(): any argument of scenario() to change. layers given here are merged into the base's layers by name (a layer set to NULL is removed).

Value

A plancap_scenario.

Details

scenario_change() starts from an existing scenario and changes only what it is given, which is how a plan change is usually described.

See also

prepare_sites()

Examples

town <- exampleton()
base <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
                 parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
                 roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
                 zoning = town$zoning,
                 layers = town[c("height_areas", "flood_hazard", "heritage",
                                 "trees", "precincts", "transit")],
                 water = town$water, centrelines = town$road_centrelines)
base
#> <plancap scenario> Operative
#> Rulebook: Exampleton District Plan; 1377 parcels; 7 zoning features; layers:
#> height_areas, flood_hazard, heritage, trees, precincts, transit.
taller <- scenario_change(base, "MDR at 16 m",
  rulebook = set_rule(base$rulebook, "zones.MDR.height.value", 16))
